nodes.label: FaceAttend
nodes.rationale: The current product is a deliberately small Python-first biometric attendance system, not a public-web monitoring product.

nodes.label: Explicit Self Check-In
nodes.rationale: Attendance is initiated by the user and is never recorded from a static uploaded image alone.

nodes.label: Face Registration
nodes.rationale: A consenting user records a short liveness video; a verified live frame becomes the registered face template.

nodes.label: Attendance Session
nodes.rationale: Every check-in occurs within a user-created attendance session.

nodes.label: Liveness-Gated Check-In
nodes.rationale: Active liveness, passive liveness, face visibility, and identity similarity must pass before attendance is recorded.

nodes.label: Active Liveness
nodes.rationale: A MediaPipe blink and head-turn challenge provides action-based evidence that the subject is live; the backend is authoritative.

nodes.label: Passive Liveness
nodes.rationale: MiniFASNet-style spoof detection evaluates sampled frames from the same webcam video without a separate user action.

nodes.label: Registered-Template Identity Matching
nodes.rationale: Matching is constrained to the user's registered embedding; low-confidence and wrong-person results cannot record attendance.

nodes.label: Idempotent Duplicate Check-In
nodes.rationale: Repeated check-ins to the same session return a visible duplicate state instead of creating an unintended second attendance event.

nodes.label: Embedding-Only Vector Storage
nodes.rationale: The vector database stores face embeddings rather than raw face crops to minimize biometric exposure.

nodes.label: Biometric Audit Log
nodes.rationale: Every biometric operation records actor, target, action, and timestamp to support accountability and data-subject rights.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 9 Biometric Data
nodes.rationale: Face embeddings and related operations are treated as special-category biometric data requiring explicit consent, erasure, portability, and legal review.

nodes.label: Python-First Server-Rendered Frontend
nodes.rationale: FastAPI, Jinja2, and HTMX were chosen to minimize cognitive load and avoid a Node/SPA build system for a frontend beginner.

nodes.label: HTML-Fragment Web Interaction
nodes.rationale: Public-site handlers return server-rendered HTML fragments for HTMX swaps rather than acting as a JSON API.

nodes.label: Backend API Boundary
nodes.rationale: Frontend routes call backend data operations through one typed HTTP client and do not directly access databases or vector stores.

nodes.label: Webcam JavaScript Exception
nodes.rationale: Vanilla JavaScript is permitted only for webcam liveness capture; other interactivity should use HTMX unless an ADR approves expansion.

nodes.label: Legacy Crawler Search and Takedown Scope
nodes.rationale: Crawler, public-web search, monitoring, and takedown artifacts belong to a previous direction and are excluded from current attendance work unless explicitly requested.
nodes.norm_label: legacy crawler search and takedown scope

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Record Process
nodes.rationale: Significant model, privacy, retention, audit, vendor, or frontend-stack changes require a documented ADR and human sign-off.

nodes.label: Attendance Login Requirement
nodes.rationale: Attendance check-in is gated behind authentication, with explicit login and registration actions.

nodes.label: Embedding Model Version Display
nodes.rationale: The successful registration view exposes the embedding model version when registration data is present.

nodes.label: Legacy Public-Image Crawler Scope
nodes.rationale: This document describes the earlier public-web image discovery subsystem; project instructions identify crawler and takedown work as legacy relative to the attendance MVP.

nodes.label: Legacy Crawler Ingest Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The legacy pipeline schedules spiders, applies robots and rate controls, downloads images, deduplicates by perceptual hash, stores content, and emits inference jobs.

nodes.label: Crawler Proxy Pool
nodes.rationale: Proxies are intended for distribution and reliability, never to evade explicit rate limits.

nodes.label: robots.txt Compliance
nodes.rationale: Public crawling must respect robots directives; any override requires documented justification and legal sign-off.

nodes.label: Crawler Politeness Policy
nodes.rationale: The legacy crawler is limited to public URLs and a default maximum of one request per second per domain.

nodes.label: Crawler Perceptual-Hash Deduplication
nodes.rationale: URL dedup is the cheap first layer; pHash content dedup avoids storing duplicate bytes while retaining last-seen information.

nodes.label: Legacy Re-Crawl Priorities
nodes.rationale: Legacy re-crawl frequency increases for pages with monitored-user matches or high image churn and decreases for stable archives.

nodes.label: Legacy Source-Level Takedown Handling
nodes.rationale: A source takedown request requires blocklisting the domain, purging indexed content, and recording the reason.

nodes.label: Current Attendance API Scope
nodes.rationale: The target public API centers on authentication, face registrations, explicit check-ins, attendance records, and user data rights.

nodes.label: Redis-Backed Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Per-route limits vary by authentication and plan status and use Redis as shared enforcement state.

nodes.label: Liveness Before Registration and Check-In
nodes.rationale: Every face registration and check-in must validate liveness before face inference or attendance-related matching proceeds.

nodes.label: Face Registration Flow
nodes.rationale: Audit the attempt, verify liveness, detect and embed the face, index the embedding with its model version, then audit success.

nodes.label: VectorStore Protocol
nodes.rationale: All vector database operations are isolated behind one interface so FAISS, Milvus, or Qdrant can be selected at startup.

nodes.label: Versioned 512-Dimensional Face Embedding
nodes.rationale: Embeddings are 512-dimensional float32 vectors, normalized at ingest and stored with provenance and model-version metadata.

nodes.label: Append-Only Biometric Audit Log
nodes.rationale: Every biometric operation is auditable through an append-only PostgreSQL record containing actor, action, target, request context, and timestamp.

nodes.label: Biometric Data Minimization
nodes.rationale: Raw face crops and client-visible embeddings are prohibited; vector storage holds embeddings while relational storage holds links and metadata.

nodes.label: Legacy Backend Takedown Workflow
nodes.rationale: The document retains an older DMCA notice and platform-reporting workflow that is separate from the current attendance product scope.

nodes.label: ADR Decision Rationale
nodes.rationale: An architecture decision records context, alternatives, the chosen decision, consequences, and references.

nodes.label: Current Enrollment and Search Pipeline
nodes.rationale: User-submitted biometric input is rejected unless it passes liveness and face detection before alignment and embedding.

nodes.label: Legacy ML Crawler Ingest Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The older crawler path hashes and deduplicates public images, detects and embeds faces, assigns clusters, and writes a vector index without liveness because the images were not user check-ins.

nodes.label: SCRFD-10G Face Detection
nodes.rationale: SCRFD-10G is the default detector because it is fast, accurate, and ONNX-friendly.

nodes.label: Five-Point Face Alignment
nodes.rationale: A standard deterministic similarity transform aligns faces before embedding.

nodes.label: ArcFace R100 Embedding
nodes.rationale: ArcFace R100 is the default embedding model because it is an industry-standard, well-benchmarked choice.

nodes.label: MiniFASNet v2 Passive Liveness
nodes.rationale: MiniFASNet v2 is the lightweight default passive liveness model; a low score falls back to active challenge-response.

nodes.label: MediaPipe Active Liveness
nodes.rationale: Active liveness verifies a requested blink, turn, or smile and requires the same face throughout the short video.

nodes.label: Deepfake Liveness Check
nodes.rationale: A still-to-be-evaluated EfficientNet-based classifier is intended to reject obvious AI-generated faces on both passive and active inputs.

nodes.label: FAR and FRR Liveness Calibration
nodes.rationale: Default thresholds are conservative and must be recalibrated against project false-accept and false-reject targets after model changes.

nodes.label: Embedding Model Versioning
nodes.rationale: Embeddings from different models are not comparable, so writes carry a model version, searches filter by it, and upgrades require dual-write plus re-embedding.

nodes.label: Legacy Face Identity Clustering
nodes.rationale: The prior public-image workflow grouped faces online by centroid similarity and periodically refined clusters offline for result aggregation and moderation.

nodes.label: Legacy Perceptual Image Hashing
nodes.rationale: pHash identifies duplicate or modified copies of crawled images, including cases where the visible face changes or disappears.

nodes.label: Triton Inference Serving
nodes.rationale: Triton is the preferred production serving path due to GPU engines, dynamic batching, CPU fallback, and hot reload.

nodes.label: Ray Serve Inference Serving
nodes.rationale: Ray Serve is the simpler development or small-scale path because it is easier to debug and has lower operational overhead.

nodes.label: ML Model Benchmark Gate
nodes.rationale: Detection, embedding, and liveness models must produce latency, throughput, and accuracy results before promotion; quantization also requires accuracy validation.

nodes.label: Synthetic ML Test Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Repository face fixtures are synthetic so real biometric data is not committed.

nodes.label: ArcFace
nodes.description: CVPR 2019 additive angular-margin loss for discriminative face-recognition embeddings.

nodes.label: InsightFace buffalo_l
nodes.description: InsightFace model pack used by the current embedding pipeline; distributed model/data licensing is restricted to non-commercial research unless separately licensed.

nodes.label: Silent Face Anti-Spoofing
nodes.description: Upstream MiniFASNet implementation; its published inference combines multiple scales/models and warns that performance depends on camera and scene domain.

nodes.label: MiniFASNetV2
nodes.description: Compact passive presentation-attack-detection model used by the local ML service as a single ONNX model.

nodes.label: MediaPipe Face Landmarker
nodes.description: Landmark runtime used for active blink and head-turn challenges; VIDEO mode requires monotonically increasing timestamps.

nodes.label: ISO IEC 30107-3
nodes.description: Standard covering testing and reporting of biometric presentation-attack detection.

nodes.label: APCER and BPCER
nodes.description: Attack and bona-fide presentation classification error rates needed for PAD evaluation, reported by attack type and operating point.

nodes.label: OULU-NPU
nodes.description: Mobile face anti-spoofing video benchmark with official protocols and controlled-access terms; candidate for protocol-based evaluation, not yet adopted.

nodes.label: Replay-Attack
nodes.description: Presentation-attack video benchmark catalogued by NIST; candidate baseline dataset, not yet adopted.

nodes.label: CelebA-Spoof
nodes.description: Large face anti-spoofing dataset with rich annotations; official paper is the authoritative reference and unverified Hub mirrors should not be treated as licensed sources.

nodes.label: GAC-FAS
nodes.description: CVPR 2024 cross-domain face anti-spoofing work demonstrating that domain generalization remains an active evaluation problem.

nodes.label: NIST Demographic Effects
nodes.description: NIST evidence that face-recognition error rates can vary with image quality and demographics motivates subgroup and image-quality evaluation.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 9
nodes.description: Biometric data used for unique identification is special-category data; explicit consent is one conditional exception, not an automatic lawful basis in every context.

nodes.label: Attendance Consent Power Imbalance
nodes.description: Employment or education attendance can involve power imbalance; official EU guidance and enforcement show that consent may not be freely given or legally sufficient.

nodes.label: Threshold Calibration
nodes.description: Recognition and active/passive liveness thresholds require target-camera, attack-type, demographic, and operating-point validation before deployment.
